statement: For a based loop commuting with an actual closed free proper one-dimensional operator group on a plane, the principal base common fixed set gives a complete orbit decomposition. Each complementary base interval is either one open orbit strip or a strip of continuous parallel graphs with the displayed exact conjugacy and actual effective-image topology. At fixed base points the orbits are horizontal lines or individual points. Each actual finite-endpoint translation character has zero or full-real image on a base-point stabilizer; in the zero case a nonzero character gives the stated real translation coordinate on the base. The original component operators, comparison kernel and source words are retained.
depends_on: C33 actual principal action coordinate and all component normal forms; the C62 word triangle and zero-set argument, whose exact hypotheses are verified again here for the actual finite-word paths; compact word evaluation and the explicit graph, source and inverse maps proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), exact one-dimensional proper-operator orbit and frontier reduction.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The proof uses the actual group generated by the original loop, with explicit paths to every finite word. No replacement by a closure is made. The continuous graph is proved through compact evaluation intervals, and all original component labels and the endpoint comparison-action kernel remain explicit.
computational_checks: This is a qualitative orbit and topology theorem. Its group, conjugacy and inverse formulas are proved directly; no finite or numerical classification is used.
notes: The graph is proper only in its specified open strip, and its endpoint extension is not asserted. The effective restricted image has the stated topology, but no quotient-topology assertion for the original global restriction map is made. Full-real endpoint correction is an actual source-word surjectivity statement, not a continuous section. Boundary-compatible contraction across nonfixed interior lines and the original disk circle remains unresolved in C12.
